title: Automate tenant RBAC rotation and safe rollback hooks for Private installer
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Private deployments require periodic rotation of tenant bootstrap credentials and a reliable rollback surface for RBAC changes applied by the installer. This PR automates tenant RBAC rotation (Terraform + Helm) and adds safe rollback hooks and validation checks to the private installer so upgrades don't leave tenants in an inconsistent state. Motivation: previous manual steps during upgrades caused transient permission gaps and one post-upgrade incident where tenant agent registration failed (SUP-1287). Goal: make RBAC seed and rotation idempotent, introduce a transactional Helm hook for rollback capture, and add pre-upgrade dry-run checks that detect potential permission drift. Summary of changes: 1) Terraform module updates: add tenant_rbac_rotation module (modules/tenant_rbac_rotation/) which exposes an idempotent apply plan, a rotation window parameter, and outputs a rotation_plan_id for audit; make the Terraform provider usage explicit to avoid implicit ordering issues. 2) Helm chart (charts/private-installer): add pre-upgrade Job hook templates that snapshot current ClusterRoleBindings and Namespaces affected by tenant policies into a ConfigMap (rotations/snapshots) and a post-install Job that validates post-change bindings; include a hook to write a rollback manifest in S3-compatible objectstore if running in air-gapped mode use PVC. 3) Installer orchestration: add orchestration step to run Terraform rotation plan, verify snapshot checksums, and reconcile if drift detected; make the step tolerant to transient API rate limits and retry with exponential backoff. 4) Rollback tooling: new script tools/rollback-rbac.sh (invoked by the Helm hook) which can apply the captured rollback manifest or replay Terraform state to restore pre-upgrade RBAC. 5) Observability and audit: emit in-console events and add two team-level metrics (rbac.rotation.start and rbac.rotation.success) and a trace span in the upgrade pipeline. 6) Tests and safety: unit tests for Terraform helpers, Helm lint and chart tests, e2e scenario in perf-canary that simulates tenant creation + rotation. How this is different: unlike previous one-off bootstrap scripts, this change ties Terraform and Helm lifecycle together and captures a concrete rollback artifact for each upgrade. Idempotency and clear audit IDs are key. Developer checklist: - [x] Implement Terraform module with idempotent apply - [x] Add Helm hook templates and rollback script - [x] Wire orchestration in installer main upgrade path - [x] Add metrics and tracing hooks - [x] Add unit, lint and e2e tests - [x] Update private-installer docs (upgrade guide) Testing notes: CI initially failed due to a race in the pre-upgrade Job (k8s API list RBAC returned partial fields); fixed by increasing list timeout and adding field filtering. Full CI run: terraform fmt/lint pass, helm lint pass, unit tests pass, integration e2e (canary) pass. Security review: scoped service account for the rotation job minimizes blast radius; rotation credentials are written to ephemeral Secrets encrypted with the cluster KMS; audit log entries include rotation_plan_id. Rollback plan for customers: the installer now writes a rollback bundle to the configured objectstore or cluster ConfigMap; operators can invoke tools/rollback-rbac.sh or run the Terraform replay to restore. Backwards compatibility/migration: upgrade path includes a preflight that warns if existing tenants do not support rotation (old agent versions); operator can run an opt-in flag to enable rotation per tenant. Release notes: see release_notes field. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: network partition prevents writing the rollback artifact; mitigation: installer falls back to writing into a cluster PVC and errors early to prevent proceeding. - Risk: Terraform state drift between operator runs; mitigation: rotation_plan_id and state fingerprinting added to ensure consistent application. Follow-ups: - Add an opt-out toggle for clusters with external RBAC managed by third-party controllers (DES-72) - Extend rotation to include service account token lifetime enforcement (ENG-4481).

review_comments: Liam Chen (2026-02-16): Please add a short TTL for the ConfigMap snapshots so we don't accumulate garbage in long-lived clusters; also prefer using server-side apply for the rollback manifest to reduce merge conflicts.

Priya Desai (2026-02-17): Can we avoid storing rotation credentials in Secrets if the cluster is configured with HSM-backed KMS? Suggest encrypting the blob and storing only a reference in the Secret.

Samir Kapoor (2026-02-18): The Terraform module is great but the apply order might still race with CRD installs in fresh clusters; recommend adding an explicit depends_on for tenant CRD creation or gate via helm test.
Security review (Elaine Morris, 2026-02-18): scoped SA is good. Please ensure the rotation job logs DO NOT echo full credentials; redact in logs.
author_responses: Asha Patel (2026-02-17): Added ttl_seconds parameter to snapshot ConfigMap and used server-side apply for rollback manifest (see modules/tenant_rbac_rotation/README.md).
Asha Patel (2026-02-18): Switched to KMS-encrypt-then-store flow when KMS is configured; added unit tests for encryption shim.
Asha Patel (2026-02-19): Added depends_on for tenant CRD to the module and a helm test gating step for fresh clusters.
Asha Patel (2026-02-20): Redacted logs and added an integration test asserting no secret material appears in container logs.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after second successful CI run. Final changelog includes new Terraform module, Helm hooks, rollback tooling and docs. Deployed to internal canary cluster and validated with simulated tenant rotations.
release_notes: Private installer: automated tenant RBAC rotation and safe rollback hooks. Adds a new modules/tenant_rbac_rotation Terraform module, Helm pre-upgrade/post-install hooks to snapshot RBAC state, and operator-facing rollback tooling (tools/rollback-rbac.sh). Rolling upgrade includes preflight checks and opt-in per-tenant rotation flag. No breaking changes by default; operators must opt-in to rotation for older agents.
notes_for_ops: How to trigger a rotation: 1) kubectl -n redwood-system annotate upgrade rotation=true; 2) monitor metric rbac.rotation.* and check the rotation_plan_id in the installer logs. To rollback: run tools/rollback-rbac.sh --from=rotation_plan_id or apply the captured rollback manifest from the cluster ConfigMap 'rbac-rotation-snapshots-<plan id>'.
qa_playbook: 1) Run canary: create tenant, verify agent registration. 2) Enable rotation, run upgrade flow. 3) Confirm post-upgrade agent registration and RBAC bindings match pre-upgrade snapshot. 4) Simulate failure by deleting post-install Job and run tools/rollback-rbac.sh to validate restore. 5) Verify metrics rbac.rotation.success increments and no secrets appear in logs.
notes: This PR is part of the wider Private automation initiative; it coordinates with chart maintainers and the Terraform team.
